text.moon: The batteries ran dry and the heaters died. Real lunar bases need huge energy reserves to survive two-week nights.
text.mars: The batteries ran dry. On Mars, dust storms can block sunlight for weeks, so reserves are everything.

F.title: OUT OF FOOD
F.text: The pantry is empty. Bases far from Earth must grow food locally because resupply is slow and expensive.

W.title: OUT OF WATER
W.text: Water means drinking, oxygen, farming and shielding. That's why finding ice matters so much.

R.title: RADIATION SICKNESS
R.text: Shielding failed. Without Earth's magnetic field and thick atmosphere, protection has to be built.

M.title: CREW MUTINY
M.text: Morale collapsed and the crew voted to go home. Mental health is as critical as physical health.

C.title: LOST CONTACT
C.text: Mission Control lost the signal and called off the mission. Reliable comms keep crews safe.

H.title: COLONY LOST
H.text: Too many crew members got sick or hurt to keep the base running. Health is the ultimate resource.

tips.P: Power is low. Skip power-hungry projects and look for energy gains.
tips.F: Food is low. Greenhouse choices help, even if they cost power.
tips.W: Water is low. Ice expeditions and recycler repairs are your friends.
tips.R: Shielding is weak. Dig in or shelter from flares.
tips.M: Morale is sagging. Rest, treats and calls home keep people going.
tips.C: Comms are shaky. Relays and antennas reconnect you with Earth.
tips.H: Crew health is dropping. Medical care, oxygen and exercise matter now.

aria.night: It's lunar night, so the solar panels are dead. Every multi-day project burns stored power.
aria.storm: The dust storm is eating power and comms every sol. Quick choices help.
aria.nominal: All systems nominal. Remember that long projects cost more than resources: every extra {D} drains supplies.
aria.gambleHint: This one's a gamble, about {pct}% odds.
